clue.text: Full charge for travelling open road

parts.note: thorough means complete, full in every detail
a fare is the price paid for a journey

explanation.surface: A traveller grumbles about paying the full ticket price to use a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A thoroughfare is a public street that is open at both ends to traffic.

clue.text: Bun consumed when cycling, put on coat

indicators.note: cycling moves the end letter of the word for consumed round to the front

parts.note: ate means consumed
to cake is to cover with a thick coating

explanation.surface: A cyclist eats a bun, then pulls on a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacake is a light sweet bun, often with currants, served toasted.

clue.text: Dirty old book consulted in audition

indicators.note: audition means hearing, so the word is taken by how it is heard

parts.note: to have seen a doctor is to have consulted one

explanation.surface: A dirty old book is consulted during an audition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in audition' says SEEN is heard, giving SCENE.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means indecent or filthy, as dirty jokes are.

clue.text: Go past snail sadly lost in insurmountable ground

indicators.note: the letters of the creature are lost from the long word, taken out of its pool
ground means crushed and broken up, so the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A snail is sadly lost on impassable terrain.
explanation.walkthrough: Take SNAIL's letters out of INSURMOUNTABLE; 'ground' rearranges the rest, URMOUNTBE.
explanation.definitionFit: To outnumber is to exceed in number, surpassing or going past another count.

clue.text: Mirror informant changes sides

indicators.note: the right side letter is swapped for the left side letter

parts.note: a grass is British slang for a police informer

explanation.surface: A tabloid informant defects to the other camp.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) becomes L (left). Mirror is also a British newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass is a looking glass, an old word for a mirror.

clue.text: Female sick, not going to make it

parts.note: ailing means ill

explanation.surface: A sick woman is not expected to survive.
explanation.definitionFit: Something failing is in decline and unlikely to succeed.

clue.text: Wine in box with lid off upended

indicators.note: in a down answer, upended turns the remaining letters bottom to top
the lid is the top, so the opening letter of the container goes

parts.note: a canister is a box-like container

explanation.surface: Wine is kept in a box that is opened and tipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: CANISTER loses C to give ANISTER, which 'upended' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Some acquired kids and oxen, paid anything to be involved

indicators.note: the two pieces are involved, wrapped up inside the oxen word

parts.note: steers are young castrated oxen
PD is the abbreviation for paid
aught is an old word for anything

explanation.surface: A farmer bought children and oxen, paying whatever it took.
explanation.definitionFit: Stepdaughters are gained by marriage rather than birth, acquired children.

clue.text: Band with zero sex appeal upset arrangement

parts.note: an orchestra is a band of musicians

indicators.note: upset tips over the phrase for zero sex appeal so it reads upwards

parts.note: no means none, zero
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: An unattractive band is upset by an arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchestration is the arranging of music for an orchestra.

clue.text: Reverse van route

definitions.meaning: in surveying, to ... a theodolite is to turn its telescope over, reversing it
the Ford ... is a familiar make of van
the passage or way from one place to another

explanation.surface: Directions to back a delivery vehicle along its route.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions in three words; the surveying sense of 'Reverse' is the obscure one.
explanation.definitionFit: Each word names one sense: the surveying verb, the Ford van model, and passage across a place.

clue.text: Flier advanced to Rome's edge following Roman road

indicators.note: the words before it come after the Roman road in the answer

parts.note: via is Latin for road, as in the Via Appia

indicators.note: the edge of the word Rome's here is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone advances to the outskirts of Rome along an ancient highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' governs only the part after 'advanced': the Roman road comes first, then the rest, while A heads the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviator is a pilot, someone who flies aircraft.

clue.text: Level out denture with gold

parts.note: a dental plate is a set of false teeth
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A dentist sets out a set of false teeth with gold fillings.
explanation.definitionFit: To plateau is to stop rising and stay at a steady level, as a graph flattening.

clue.text: Piggy is stylish around home

indicators.note: the stylish word goes round the home word, enclosing it

parts.note: swish is informal for smart or fashionable
in means at home

explanation.surface: A pig-like person turns out to be quite fashionable around the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Swinish means like a pig, coarse or greedy, as piggy does.

clue.text: Songstress directed backing in American English

indicators.note: the reversed word sits inside the abbreviation

parts.note: AE is the abbreviation for American English

indicators.note: backing turns the word for directed round to read the other way

parts.note: led means guided or directed

explanation.surface: A singer is guided by backing vocals in an American accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like musical support, but it turns LED into DEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Adele is the British singer-songwriter famous for Hello and Someone Like You.

clue.text: Country music from sad dope

parts.note: blue means sad or down
grass is slang for cannabis, which dope also means

explanation.surface: Country music produced by a melancholy stoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluegrass is a style of American country music played on banjo and fiddle.

clue.text: Turned out to consume tea that's unfamiliar

indicators.note: the rearranged word eats the tea word, holding it inside
out means wrong or disordered, so the preceding word is rearranged

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: Someone turned up to drink unfamiliar tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TURNED into UNRTED, which takes in CHA.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncharted territory is unexplored, so strange and unknown.

clue.text: 'Simply patterned' encountered in Virgilian poem, not good the second time

indicators.note: the word for encountered goes inside the shortened poem
not tells us to leave the letter for good out of the poem

parts.note: the Georgics are Virgil's poems on farming; one is a Georgic
G is the abbreviation for good; the second time means its second occurrence in the poem goes
met means encountered

explanation.surface: A quoted phrase about simple patterns turns up in Virgil, though not as good on repeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes only the poem's second G, the 'second time' good appears in it, leaving GEORIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Geometric patterns use simple regular shapes such as lines, circles and squares.

clue.text: Have something in common with friend, literally?

parts.note: read as an instruction, the answer says put LAP over, turning it backwards, which spells the word for friend, pal

explanation.surface: Asks whether sharing something with a friend is meant literally.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer is the wordplay and the clue word is its result.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things overlap when they partly coincide, sharing some ground.

clue.text: Nearly nuts about Oscar after a short time

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about the letter for Oscar
nuts means crazy, so the word before it is jumbled

parts.note: Oscar is O in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone nearly goes mad over an Oscar shortly after starting out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' turns NEARLY into EARLYN, with O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Early on describes the opening period, soon after something begins.

clue.text: Curse witches wearing clothes

indicators.note: clothes is read as a verb, covers: the two words wrap the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A curse is put on witches wearing particular clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear is to utter a curse or profanity.

clue.text: Warriors mostly told to surround an odd revolutionary

indicators.note: the shortened word goes round the turned phrase
mostly drops the last letter of the word for told

parts.note: said means told

indicators.note: revolutionary turns the phrase for an odd round

parts.note: rum means strange or odd

explanation.surface: Warriors were told to surround a strange rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: SAID less D is SAI; A RUM turned is MURA.
explanation.definitionFit: Samurai were the warrior class of feudal Japan; the plural is the same as the singular.

clue.text: Observe line has disturbed facial feature

parts.note: to eye is to observe

indicators.note: disturbed means stirred up, so the letters of the little word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone notices that a wrinkle has spoilt their face.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelash is one of the hairs fringing the eyelid, part of the face.

clue.text: Article indicator of alternative space hypothesis

parts.note: the is the definite article
or is the word that signals an alternative
an em is a printer's unit of space

explanation.surface: A paper sets out an alternative theory of space.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorem is a proposition to be proved, close to a hypothesis put forward.

clue.text: Morse vacantly needing help to raise sources of information

indicators.note: vacantly empties the name of its inside, keeping only its first and last letters
in a down answer, to raise lifts the word so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: Inspector Morse, looking blank, needs help to find his sources.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse is a British TV detective; 'to raise' turns AID into DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The media are the press and broadcasters, channels supplying news and information.

clue.text: Ready to explode? Nap in part of chair

parts.note: to arm a bomb is to make it ready to explode
a nap is a short rest

explanation.surface: Someone at breaking point takes a nap in a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: An armrest is the side support of a chair for resting the arm on.

clue.text: Amateur entering pipe operated in shifts

indicators.note: the amateur word goes into the pipe word

parts.note: a reed is a simple musical pipe
lay means non-professional, amateur

explanation.surface: An amateur plumber gets inside a pipe and works on it in turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A relay is a team working in turns, so relayed means worked in shifts.

clue.text: Storm split again around area

indicators.note: the first two pieces go around the letter for area

parts.note: torn means split or ripped
do, short for ditto, means the same again

explanation.surface: A storm tears through a region once more.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating windstorm.

clue.text: Golf tournament, also location for snack

parts.note: the Open is golf's British championship
Sandwich in Kent, home of Royal St George's, is a location for the Open

explanation.surface: A golf tournament that doubles as a venue for a bite to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: SANDWICH is a Kent town whose links course hosts the Open.
explanation.definitionFit: An open sandwich is a single slice of bread with a topping, a light meal or snack.
